purpose: One combined source-first inventory covering the 66 Area-2 decision paths that B3-C and B3-D together require, so B3-C does not finish only for B3-D to discover no remaining capacity.

method.granularity: CMR paragraph / statutory subsection, not regulation number
method.area_assignment_rule: Classify from the actual tested competency and existing bank precedent, never from the regulation number. A source is not usable merely because it is unused.
method.verbatim_rule: The controlling proposition must be verbatim-verifiable from an official primary or official government source before authoring. Section headings, corrupted partial text, secondary republication alone and search snippets alone are all rejected.

source_viability.publisher: Commonwealth of Massachusetts, official publisher of the General Laws
source_viability.retrieval: Browser, same-origin fetch, section text under the main paragraph nodes
source_viability.evidence: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19 retrieved in full and verbatim, including subsections (a) through (d). Subsection (a) states that a prescription for a controlled substance to be valid shall be issued for a legitimate medical purpose by a practitioner acting in the usual course of his professional practice, and that a corresponding responsibility shall rest with the pharmacist who fills the prescription.
source_viability.significance: This is the principal remaining Area-2 source. M.G.L. c. 94C and c. 112 pharmacist-practice provisions are fully available at paragraph granularity.
source_viability.note_on_urls: Section URLs that carry a fraction in the section number, for example c. 112 s. 24B one-half, do not resolve under the naive tilde-two encoding and must be located from the chapter index.

source_viability.evidence: Section 9.15(1) and (2) retrieved verbatim and used to repair MA-Q-0288.
source_viability.area_capacity_finding: Largely exhausted as an Area-2 source. Bank precedent puts 9.02 and 9.04 in Area 4, 9.14 and 9.17 in Area 3, 9.19 and 9.24 in Area 4, and 9.21 and 9.23 in Area 1. Of the sections with no question at all, compliance packaging, emergency kits, automated systems, records, non-resident pharmacies, storage, plans of correction and generic interchange all sit in Area 4 by precedent. Clearly Area-2 headroom is limited to 9.03 Advertising plus unkeyed paragraphs of 9.01, 9.13 and 9.15.

source_viability.source: 247 CMR 16.00 Collaborative Drug Therapy Management via mass.gov official PDF
source_viability.detail: 18 of 34 compressed streams decompress. Sections 16.01 and 16.02 extract cleanly and match text independently confirmed earlier. Section 16.03 and parts of 16.04 recover only with severe kerning fragmentation, for example 'm us t pr ov ide tha t th e su pe rv isi ng ph y sic ia n'. Probes for the termination terms and for the agreement filed in the primary practice setting return nothing, so parts of 16.04 are absent from the extraction.
source_viability.controller_decision: Do NOT author 16.03 or 16.04 propositions from this extraction. De-kerned text is reconstruction, not verbatim verification, and the governing instruction forbids authoring from corrupted partial text. An alternative official rendering must be found before 16.03 and 16.04 can be counted toward Area-2 capacity.
source_viability.impact: 247 CMR 16.04 is the single richest untapped CDTM source, covering required agreement terms, duties, biennial renewal, termination, filing in the primary practice setting and employment relationships. Losing it materially reduces the Area-2 candidate pool, so its recovery is a priority for the remainder of the census.

capacity_position.assessment: Not yet answerable. Source viability is established for the statutes, which is the decisive enabler, but the paragraph-level path inventory across M.G.L. c. 94C, M.G.L. c. 112, 105 CMR 700.000 and the recoverable parts of 247 CMR 16.00 has not been completed. No B3-C drafting has begun and none will begin until the census demonstrates at least 66 defensible distinct Area-2 decision paths.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.exact_section: 24B1/2(a), definition of collaborative drug therapy management
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: CDTM is the initiating, monitoring, modifying and discontinuing of a patient's drug therapy by a pharmacist in accordance with a collaborative practice agreement; it may include collecting and reviewing patient histories, obtaining and checking vital signs, and, under the supervision of or in direct consultation with a physician, ordering and evaluating the results of laboratory tests directly related to drug therapy when performed in accordance with approved protocols applicable to the practice setting and when the evaluation shall not include a diagnostic component.
paths.trigger: pharmacist proposes to order or interpret a laboratory test while co-managing therapy
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide whether the proposed act falls inside CDTM or crosses into diagnosis
conditions: under physician supervision or in direct consultation
test directly related to drug therapy
performed under approved protocols applicable to the practice setting
exceptions: the evaluation shall not include a diagnostic component
paths.why_area_2: Tests the outer boundary of the pharmacist's own professional practice, which is Area 2 competency, not facility operations or a dispensing mechanic.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: A collaborative practice agreement is a written and signed agreement between a pharmacist with training and experience relevant to the scope of the collaborative practice and a supervising physician that defines the collaborative practice. The collaborative practice shall be within the scope of the supervising physician's practice. Each collaborative practice agreement shall be subject to review and renewal on a biennial basis. A collaborative practice agreement shall include individually developed guidelines for any prescriptive practice of the pharmacist.
paths.trigger: an agreement is drafted, or is reaching its second anniversary
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide whether the agreement is validly constituted and still current
conditions: within the supervising physician's own scope of practice
individually developed guidelines for any prescriptive practice
paths.why_area_2: Turns on the pharmacist's authority to act at all, which is a practice-competency question.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: A patient is a person referred to a pharmacist by his supervising physician for the purpose of receiving CDTM services. The supervising physician shall assess the patient and include a diagnosis when referring the patient to the collaborating pharmacist. The patient shall be notified of, and shall consent to, the CDTM services in the retail drug business setting. Individual referral and consent shall be recorded by the pharmacist and the supervising physician in the patient's record.
paths.trigger: a person presents for CDTM services without a completed referral or recorded consent
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide whether this person is a CDTM patient the pharmacist may co-manage
conditions: physician assessment and diagnosis in the referral
notice and consent in the retail drug business setting
referral and consent recorded by BOTH pharmacist and physician in the patient record
exceptions: the express notice-and-consent limb is written for the retail drug business setting
paths.why_area_2: The pharmacist must decide whether a patient in front of them is eligible for their own service.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.exact_section: 24B1/2(c)(1) through (4), non-retail settings and their approval authorities
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: CDTM shall only be allowed in the following settings: hospitals licensed under c. 111 s. 51, subject to approval by the medical staff executive committee or designee; long-term care facilities licensed under c. 111 s. 71, subject to approval by the medical director or designee; inpatient or outpatient hospice settings licensed under c. 111 s. 57D, subject to approval by the hospice's medical director or designee; ambulatory care clinics licensed under c. 111 s. 51, with on-site supervision by the attending physician and a collaborating pharmacist, subject to approval by the medical staff executive committee or designee, or medical director or designee.
paths.trigger: a CDTM arrangement is proposed in a particular care setting
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: identify whose approval the setting requires and whether on-site supervision applies
conditions: setting must be one of the enumerated licensed settings
the approving body differs by setting
ambulatory care clinics additionally require on-site supervision by the attending physician and a collaborating pharmacist
paths.why_area_2: The pharmacist decides whether they may practise CDTM here and on whose authority; this is scope of the pharmacist's own practice rather than facility licensure.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: A collaborating pharmacist in a retail drug business, with supervision by a physician according to the terms of the collaborative practice agreement, is limited to patients 18 years of age or older and to an extension by 30 days of current drug therapy prescribed by the supervising physician.
paths.actor: collaborating pharmacist in a retail drug business
paths.trigger: a referred retail patient needs continued therapy or is under 18
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide whether the patient and the proposed extension are inside the retail limits
conditions: patients 18 years of age or older
the therapy extended must be current therapy prescribed by the supervising physician
paths.why_area_2: A pharmacist-side authority limit exercised at the point of care.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.exact_section: 24B1/2(c)(5), retail disease-state list and specific reference requirement
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: In the retail setting the collaborating pharmacist is limited to administration of vaccines or the modification of dosages of medications prescribed by the supervising physician for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, congestive heart failure, HIV or AIDS, osteoporosis and co-morbidities identified by the supervising physician for the individual patient along with the primary diagnosis. The collaborative practice agreement shall specifically reference each disease state being co-managed.
paths.actor: collaborating pharmacist in a retail drug business
paths.trigger: a dosage modification is proposed for a condition
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide whether the condition is inside the retail list and specifically referenced in the agreement
conditions: condition on the enumerated list, or a co-morbidity identified by the physician for that patient
the agreement must specifically reference each disease state co-managed
paths.why_area_2: A clinical-authority boundary the pharmacist applies personally.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: A retail drug business practicing in collaborative drug therapy management under this section shall not be required to register as a Health Facility under 105 CMR 700.004(A)(2)(d).
paths.actor: retail drug business engaging in CDTM
paths.trigger: a pharmacy is advised it must add a Health Facility registration before starting CDTM
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide whether the additional registration is in fact required
exceptions: the carve-out applies to a retail drug business practising CDTM under this section
paths.why_area_2: Borderline. The proposition is about a registration obligation rather than a pharmacist practice decision, which points at Area 4 by bank precedent for facility registration items.
paths.rejection_reason: Classified Area 4, not Area 2. Facility registration obligations sit with pharmacy operations in this bank. Not counted toward the Area-2 total.

paths.source: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 (Pharmacist collaborative practice agreements; collaborative drug therapy management)
paths.verbatim_operative_proposition: A physician or a physician group may hire pharmacists for the purpose of practicing collaborative drug therapy management under a collaborative practice agreement for the benefit of a patient of that physician or physician group. No retail pharmacy may employ a physician for the purpose of maintaining, establishing or entering into a collaborative practice agreement with a patient. Nothing shall prohibit a retail pharmacy from hiring a physician or licensed medical practitioner for the purpose of conducting quality assurance reviews of its pharmacists that are engaged in the practice of collaborative drug therapy.
paths.actor: collaborating pharmacist and the employing entity
paths.trigger: a retail pharmacy proposes to employ a physician in connection with CDTM
paths.pharmacist_decision_or_action: decide which direction of employment the statute permits and for what purpose
conditions: physician or physician group may hire pharmacists for CDTM
exceptions: a retail pharmacy may hire a physician for quality assurance review of its CDTM pharmacists, but not for maintaining, establishing or entering into a collaborative practice agreement
paths.why_area_2: The prohibition governs the integrity of the pharmacist's collaborative practice, which the pharmacist must be able to apply; the bank places professional-conduct limits in Area 2.

gate_status: 7/66 confirmed. B3-C drafting has NOT begun and will not begin until the count reaches at least 66.

source_classification_surveys.survey: M.G.L. c. 94C pharmacist-facing sections and the c. 112 pharmacy index
source_classification_surveys.retrieved_from: malegislature.gov, official publisher of the General Laws, verbatim section text
source_classification_surveys.finding: Most of c. 94C's pharmacist-facing content classifies to Area 3 Dispensing Requirements by this bank's precedent, not to Area 2 Pharmacist Practice. Area 2 in this bank means the pharmacist's own professional practice: counselling, administration, pharmacist prescribing, validity determinations as professional judgment, professional conduct and public-health roles. It does not mean dispensing mechanics.

source_classification_surveys.risk_flagged_early: The Area-2 vein is real but narrower than the raw volume of unused source text suggests, because much of that text classifies to Areas 1, 3 and 4. Whether 66 additional defensible Area-2 decision paths exist is a genuinely open question at this stage. It will be answered by completing the inventory, and if the answer is no the measured shortfall will be reported rather than solved by relabelling Area-3 or Area-4 content.
